title: Punjabi Devils MC Founder Gets 5+ Years for Gun Dealing
excerpt: Jashanpreet Singh, who ran a Stockton-based outlaw biker gang tied to the Hells Angels, sentenced in federal court for firearms trafficking
body:
A federal judge in Sacramento sentenced 27-year-old Jashanpreet Singh to more than five years in prison on Monday for illegally dealing firearms and possessing a machine gun — capping a case that exposed the reach of a Punjab-origin outlaw motorcycle gang deep inside California.

Singh founded the Punjabi Devils Motorcycle Club, a Stockton-based outfit affiliated with the Hells Angels. He first drew FBI attention on June 6, 2025, when he tried to sell a short-barrelled rifle, three assault weapons, three machine-gun conversion devices, and a revolver to an undercover officer. A subsequent raid on his residence turned up additional machine guns, a silencer, high-capacity drum magazines, a pineapple-style hand grenade, and what investigators believed was a military claymore mine.

**Flight and Capture:** After failing to appear in court on July 21, Singh booked a ticket to India. The FBI, tipped off by Customs and Border Protection, intercepted him at San Francisco International Airport on July 26 before he could board. He has remained in federal custody since.

**The Broader Pattern:** Singh’s case lands amid a string of high-profile prosecutions involving Punjabi-origin suspects in the United States. In the past year alone, the FBI dismantled the Pavittar Manjha Gang in California, arrested operatives linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi network, and pursued extortion rings stretching from the Central Valley to British Columbia. Law enforcement officials say outlaw motorcycle clubs — traditionally a white-dominated subculture — are increasingly drawing young Punjabi immigrants who see the clubs as pathways to fast money and street credibility.

For the estimated 700,000 Punjabi Americans concentrated in California’s Central Valley, the headlines land uncomfortably. Community leaders have repeatedly stressed that the vast majority of Punjabi immigrants are law-abiding farmworkers, truckers, and entrepreneurs, and that a handful of criminal cases risk tarring an entire community at a time when anti-immigrant sentiment is already running high.

**Legal Consequences:** Singh faced a maximum of five years for the firearms-dealing charge and ten years for the machine-gun possession charge. The US Department of Justice said the FBI’s Sacramento field office investigated the case, with prosecution handled by the Eastern District of California.

**What to Watch:** Singh’s sentencing may embolden federal prosecutors to pursue wider racketeering charges against the Punjabi Devils MC itself, a move that would mirror recent RICO cases against other outlaw motorcycle clubs across the country.
nri_angle: The case spotlights a growing pattern of Punjabi-origin youth involvement in US outlaw biker gangs, raising uncomfortable questions for the 700,000-strong Punjabi American community in California already navigating anti-immigrant sentiment.
author: Diaspora Desk
